top_choice_rationale: P001 credits the quantum spin Hall effect as one intellectual unit: the Kane-Mele Z2 prediction of helical edge states followed by Molenkamp's quantitative HgTe edge-conductance measurement, with about two decades of independent confirmation. Keeping Kane and Mele together is the allocation I can defend best, and the citation states exactly what is honoured (quantum spin Hall effect and its HgTe observation) without claiming the 3D discovery. P003 recognises the same discovery but separates Kane from Mele on the joint 2005 papers; P002 (optical lattice clocks) is mature, reproducible and cleanly credited, but I still read it as an enabling refinement of earlier metrology prizes with limited new-physics output so far. Any award is preferable to no award given the maturity on the table.
recusal_note: No conflict with the laureates in P001-P003 apparent from profile; my only strong institutional stake is circuit QED (B038) via WACQT/Chalmers, which is not on the slate. Loose WACQT tie to Kroll and shared Gothenburg environment with Mehlig and Olsson, no known collaboration.
